before.title: A maximal common development has no corresponding boundary points: the spacelike restart produces a strictly larger common development
before.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data,
let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment
([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a)),
write $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $C\subseteq\partial U$ be the set of
boundary points with a corresponding boundary point. Assume that $(U,\varphi)$
is maximal among the common subdevelopments of $M$ and $M'$ in the following
sense: for every common subdevelopment $(V,\chi)$ of $M$ and $M'$ one has
$V\subseteq U$ and $\chi=\varphi$ on $V$ (this is the maximality property of
the maximal common development, [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]] clause
(b)). Then $C=\varnothing$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data and
let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$C\subseteq\partial U$ be the set of boundary points that have a corresponding
point (clause (c) of that definition), and write $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$. If
$C\cap J^+(\Sigma)\neq\varnothing$, then there exists $p\in C\cap J^+(\Sigma)$
with
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed
boundary point in the sense of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]:
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$
Fix a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $p$
([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let
$p_1\ll p\ll p_2$ be points of $C$ such that $W:=I^+(p_1)\cap I^-(p_2)$
satisfies $\overline W\subseteq C$ (possible: strong causality at $p$ supplies
a neighbourhood $V_2\subseteq C$ of $p$ such that every causal curve with
both endpoints in $V_2$ is contained in $C$, and then
$\overline W\subseteq J^+(p_1)\cap J^-(p_2)\subseteq C$ for $p_1,p_2\in V_2$
by the same argument). Then $W$ is open, causally convex, $p\in W$, and
$\overline W$ is compact. Let $q\in W\cap I^+(p)$ be a point with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W,$$
chosen so close to $p$ along a future timelike curve that also $q\in W$
([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from
$q$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) and put
$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$
Let $W^\circ:=W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and let $S$ be the connected component of
the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in
$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(b)** $S$ is a nonempty smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface of $M$
without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap
C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(c)** There is a smooth positive function $\delta:S\to(0,\infty)$ with the
following properties. Define $X:=\nabla\tau_q/g(\nabla\tau_q,\nabla\tau_q)$
(so that $d\tau_q(X)=1$) on $\{\tau_q>0\}\cap W$, let $\phi_t$ be its local
flow, and put
$$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M,\qquad F(s,t):=\phi_t(s),\qquad N:=F\bigl(S\times(-\delta,\delta)\bigr).$$
Then $F$ is well defined and smooth, $N\subseteq W$ is open,
$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to N$ is a diffeomorphism,
$\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$, and:

1. every causal curve in $N$ is, in the coordinates $(s,t)$, of the form
   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric
   of $S$, and it meets $S$ in at most one parameter value;
2. every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets
   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;
3. for every $y\in N\cap U$ there is a unique $s\in S$ with $y=F(s,t_y)$ for
   some $t_y\in(-\delta(s),\delta(s))$, and the radial segment with the base
   point removed,
   $\{F(s,u):u\text{ between }0\text{ and }t_y,\ u\ne0\}$, is contained in
   $U$.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$$C:=\{p\in\partial U:\ p\text{ has a corresponding boundary point in }\partial\varphi(U)\}$$
be the set of boundary points of $U$ that have a corresponding point (clause
(c) of that definition). Then:

**(a)** $C$ is open in $\partial U$: there is an open set $G\subseteq M$ with
$C=G\cap\partial U$.

**(b)** There is an open set $\Omega\subseteq M$ with $U\cup C\subseteq\Omega$
and a smooth map $\Phi:\Omega\to M'$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\varphi$ and
whose value at $p\in C$ is the unique corresponding boundary point of $p$;
moreover, for every $p\in C$ there is an open neighbourhood
$W_p\subseteq\Omega$ of $p$ and a smooth **local diffeomorphism**
$$\widehat\varphi_p:W_p\to M',\qquad \widehat\varphi_p(q)=\exp_{\varphi(a_p)}\bigl(d\varphi_{a_p}(\exp_{a_p}^{-1}q)\bigr)$$
built from a common interior base point $a_p\in I^-(p)\cap U$ and the
exponential maps, such that $\widehat\varphi_p=\varphi$ on $W_p\cap U$ and
$\Phi=\widehat\varphi_p$ on $W_p\cap(U\cup C)$. No isometry property of
$\widehat\varphi_p$ on the part of $W_p$ outside $\overline U$ is claimed.

**(c)** At every point $q\in U\cup C$ the map $\Phi$ preserves the metric, the
matter fields and the metric-selected connection:

1. $g'_{\Phi(q)}(d\Phi_qv,d\Phi_qw)=g_q(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_qM$, so
   $\Phi^*(g')=g$ on $U\cup C$;
2. $(\Phi^*\psi'^i)_q=\psi^i_q$ for every listed matter field $i$;
3. for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ defined on a neighbourhood of $q$ and
   every $q\in U\cup C$,
   $$\nabla'_{d\Phi\,X}d\Phi\,Y=d\Phi\bigl(\nabla_XY\bigr)\quad\text{at }\Phi(q),$$
   equivalently the pullback connection $\Phi^*\nabla'$ equals $\nabla$ at
   $q$, where both sides are read through the invertible differential
   $d\Phi_q$.

**(d)** Every geodesic segment of $(M,g)$ whose image is contained in $U\cup C$
is mapped by $\Phi$ to a geodesic segment of $(M',g')$; a null geodesic
segment is mapped to a null geodesic segment.

**(e)** Let $S\subseteq U\cup C$ be an embedded submanifold of $M$. Then
$\Phi|_S$ is an injective immersion, hence an embedding onto its image, and it
carries the induced metric of $S$, its second fundamental form with respect to
any unit normal field, and the matter fields together with their first
covariant derivatives along $S$ to the corresponding objects of $\Phi(S)$ in
$M'$. In particular $(S,\bar g_S,k_S,\psi|_S)$ and
$(\Phi(S),\bar g_{\Phi(S)},k_{\Phi(S)},\psi'|_{\Phi(S)})$ are identified by
$\Phi|_S$ whenever $S$ is spacelike.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

Let $(W,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$S\subseteq W$ be a **partial Cauchy hypersurface**: a closed, acausal,
edgeless embedded topological hypersurface of codimension one
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], the edge being defined as
in the cited source). Write $I^\pm(S)$, $J^\pm(S)$ for the chronological and
causal future and past of $S$ in $W$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) and let
$$D^\pm(S):=\{p\in W:\ \text{every past- (respectively future-) inextendible causal curve in }W\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$$
be the **causal domains of dependence of $S$ in $W$**. Then:

**(a)** $D(S)$ is open in $W$ and $S\subseteq D(S)$; moreover
$D^\pm(S)\setminus S\subseteq I^\pm(S)$, so every point of $D(S)\setminus S$
lies on one of the two chronological sides of $S$;

**(b)** $D(S)$ is **causally convex**: every causal curve in $W$ whose
endpoints lie in $D(S)$ is contained in $D(S)$;

**(c)** $S$ is a Cauchy set of the open submanifold $(D(S),g|_{D(S)})$: every
causal curve in $D(S)$ that is inextendible in $D(S)$ meets $S$ in exactly one
parameter value.

**Data.** Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, so that $\Sigma$ is
Hausdorff, second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$,
let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, and let a **matter sector** be specified
as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a finite list of tensor types
$r_1,\dots,r_s$, a smooth **stress-energy construction** $T(g,\psi)$, a smooth
covariant symmetric $2$-tensor field built from a Lorentzian metric $g$ and
fields $\psi=(\psi^1,\dots,\psi^s)$ of the listed types on a four-manifold
carrying $\Sigma$, and a system $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that in every chart the
combined system for $(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] is a first-order quasilinear
symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on shell. Let smooth **matter initial data**
$\psi_0$ on $\Sigma$ be given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] clause (d) hold on
$\Sigma$, with $n$ the future unit normal and $T$ determined by $(h,K,\psi_0)$.
The concrete sectors used later in this batch are the vacuum sector ($s=0$,
$T=0$), the scalar-field sector ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), the
strict barotropic perfect-fluid sector ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]])
and the geodesic-dust sector ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); no other sector is
asserted here.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. smooth sections $\psi^i$ of the tensor bundles over $M$ of the types
   $r_i$ of the sector;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $\psi_0$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$, so $\varphi$ carries
   the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, that is, $\psi'{}^i(\varphi(p))=(d\varphi_p)^{\otimes}\psi^i(p)$
   for every $i$ and $p$, with the natural action on tensor fields of each
   listed type.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,\psi_0)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed
boundary point in the sense of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]:
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$
Fix a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $p$
([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let
$p_1\ll p\ll p_2$ be points of $C$ such that $W:=I^+(p_1)\cap I^-(p_2)$
satisfies $\overline W\subseteq C$ (possible: strong causality at $p$ supplies
a neighbourhood $V_2\subseteq C$ of $p$ such that every causal curve with
both endpoints in $V_2$ is contained in $C$, and then
$\overline W\subseteq J^+(p_1)\cap J^-(p_2)\subseteq C$ for $p_1,p_2\in V_2$
by the same argument). Then $W$ is open, causally convex, $p\in W$, and
$\overline W$ is compact. Let $q\in W\cap I^+(p)$ be a point with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W,$$
chosen so close to $p$ along a future timelike curve that also $q\in W$
([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from
$q$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) and put
$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$
Let $W^\circ:=W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and let $S$ be the connected component of
the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in
$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(b)** $S$ is a nonempty smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface of $M$
without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap
C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(c)** There is a smooth positive function $\delta:S\to(0,\infty)$ with the
following properties. Define $X:=\nabla\tau_q/g(\nabla\tau_q,\nabla\tau_q)$
(so that $d\tau_q(X)=1$) on $\{\tau_q>0\}\cap W$, let $\phi_t$ be its local
flow, and put
$$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M,\qquad F(s,t):=\phi_t(s),\qquad N:=F\bigl(S\times(-\delta,\delta)\bigr).$$
Then $F$ is well defined and smooth, $N\subseteq W$ is open,
$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to N$ is a diffeomorphism,
$\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$, and:

1. every causal curve in $N$ is, in the coordinates $(s,t)$, of the form
   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric
   of $S$, and it meets $S$ in at most one parameter value;
2. every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets
   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;
3. for every $y\in N\cap U$ there is a unique $s\in S$ with $y=F(s,t_y)$ for
   some $t_y\in(-\delta(s),\delta(s))$, and the radial segment with the base
   point removed,
   $\{F(s,u):u\text{ between }0\text{ and }t_y,\ u\ne0\}$, is contained in
   $U$.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause
(a), with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$. Let
$\varphi:M\to M'$ be a smooth map with $\varphi^*(g')=g$, with
$d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$ and with
$\varphi\circ j=j'$ (so $\varphi$ is an isometric immersion fixing the data).
Then:

**(a)** $d\varphi_p:T_pM\to T_{\varphi(p)}M'$ is an isomorphism for every
$p\in M$;

**(b)** $\varphi$ is injective, hence a diffeomorphism onto the open subset
$\varphi(M)\subseteq M'$ and therefore a development embedding in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c);

**(c)** if $M$ is connected and $\psi_1,\psi_2:M\to M'$ are two such
data-fixing isometric immersions, then $\psi_1=\psi_2$; in particular every
data-fixing self-isometry of a connected development is the identity of $M$.

Throughout, for a smooth map $\psi:N\to N'$ between smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds write $\psi^*(g')=g$ when $g_p(v,w)=g'_{\psi(p)}(d\psi_pv,d\psi_pw)$
for all $p\in N$ and $v,w\in T_pN$; such a map is an **isometric immersion**
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). Let $\nabla,\nabla'$ be
the metric-selected connections ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let geodesics
and exponential maps be those of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]].

**(a) Rigidity.** Let $N$ be connected and let
$\psi_1,\psi_2:N\to N'$ be isometric immersions with
$\psi_1(p)=\psi_2(p)$ and $d\psi_1(p)=d\psi_2(p)$ for some $p\in N$. Then

([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed
boundary point in the sense of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]:

([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let

satisfies $\overline W\subseteq C$ (possible: strong causality at $p$ supplies
a neighbourhood $V_2\subseteq C$ of $p$ such that every causal curve with
both endpoints in $V_2$ is contained in $C$, and then
$\overline W\subseteq J^+(p_1)\cap J^-(p_2)\subseteq C$ for $p_1,p_2\in V_2$
by the same argument). Then $W$ is open, causally convex, $p\in W$, and
$\overline W$ is compact. Let $q\in W\cap I^+(p)$ be a point with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W,$$
chosen so close to $p$ along a future timelike curve that also $q\in W$
([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from
$q$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) and put
$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$

the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap

$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric
   of $S$, and it meets $S$ in at most one parameter value;
2. every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets
   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;

   some $t_y\in(-\delta(s),\delta(s))$, and the radial segment with the base
   point removed,

([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$,
let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, and let a **matter sector** be specified
as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a finite list of tensor types
$r_1,\dots,r_s$, a smooth **stress-energy construction** $T(g,\psi)$, a smooth
covariant symmetric $2$-tensor field built from a Lorentzian metric $g$ and
fields $\psi=(\psi^1,\dots,\psi^s)$ of the listed types on a four-manifold
carrying $\Sigma$, and a system $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that in every chart the
combined system for $(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] is a first-order quasilinear
symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on shell. Let smooth **matter initial data**
$\psi_0$ on $\Sigma$ be given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] clause (d) hold on
$\Sigma$, with $n$ the future unit normal and $T$ determined by $(h,K,\psi_0)$.

$T=0$), the scalar-field sector ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), the
strict barotropic perfect-fluid sector ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]])
and the geodesic-dust sector ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); no other sector is
asserted here.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. smooth sections $\psi^i$ of the tensor bundles over $M$ of the types
   $r_i$ of the sector;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $\psi_0$.

equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$, so $\varphi$ carries
   the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, that is, $\psi'{}^i(\varphi(p))=(d\varphi_p)^{\otimes}\psi^i(p)$
   for every $i$ and $p$, with the natural action on tensor fields of each
   listed type.

into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,\psi_0)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

(Reduction to $C\cap J^+(\Sigma)
e\varnothing$; time reversal.) Suppose $C
e\varnothing$; by time reversal of the two developments (which exchanges $j(\Sigma)$-future and past and preserves all hypotheses) we may assume $C\cap J^+(\Sigma)
e\varnothing$. Then [L1] provides the exposed point $p$ and the whole restart configuration.

(The local uniqueness isometry.) By [L2] the complete Cauchy data of $S$ are realized in $M$ (by the inclusion $S\hookrightarrow M$) and in $M'$ (by $\Phi|_S$). By [L4] there is a development $D(S)\subseteq W^\circ$ of these data with Cauchy surface $S$; and applying clause (d) of [[lem-gr-local-cauchy-neighborhood]] to the smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface $\Phi(S)\subseteq M'$ (a smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface without boundary, [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] clause (e) and [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] clause (b)) gives a globally hyperbolic open neighbourhood $W_{\Phi(S)}$ of $\Phi(S)$ in $M'$ on which $\Phi(S)$ is Cauchy, hence a development of the same data with initial embedding $\Phi|_S$. The local geometric development theorem [L3] applied to these two developments yields an open neighbourhood $O\subseteq D(S)$ of $S$ and a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry $\varphi:O\to M'$ onto an open subset of $W_{\Phi(S)}$ with $\varphi|_S=\Phi|_S$ and matching all matter fields. Replace $O$ by $O\cap N$ (still an open neighbourhood of $S$, as $S\subseteq N$).

(A radial sub-tube of $O$.) Choose a continuous positive width function $\delta_0\le\delta$ on $S$ such that $\delta_0$ is Lipschitz-small with respect to the level metrics, vanishes toward the ends of $S$, and $F(s,t)\in O$ for every $|t|<\delta_0(s)$: for instance $\delta_0:=\varepsilon\min(\delta,\rho,\operatorname{dist}_h(\cdot,M\setminus O))$ with $\rho$ as in [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] and $\varepsilon>0$ small. Put $N_0:=F(S\times(-\delta_0,\delta_0))$. Then $N_0\subseteq O\cap N$ is an open radial tube over $S$.

($\psi=\varphi$ on $N_0\cap U$.) Let $y\in N_0\cap U$; write $y=F(s,t_y)$ with $s\in S$ and $|t_y|<\delta_0(s)$, and let $\gamma$ be the flow line through $s$ (a geodesic segment through $y$, [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] [L3]). By [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] clause (c)3 the radial segment from $s$ to $y$ (excluding $s$) is contained in $U$. Hence $\psi\circ\gamma$ is a geodesic of $M'$ on the parameter interval between $s$ and $y$ ([[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] clause (a)), and so is $\varphi\circ\gamma$ (as $\gamma\subseteq N_0\subseteq O$). At $s$ the two curves have the same limiting value and velocity: the value is $\Phi(s)=\varphi(s)$ (step 2.1) and the velocity is $d\varphi_s(\gamma'(s))=d\Phi_s(\gamma'(s))$, because $\varphi|_S=\Phi|_S$ gives equality on $T_sS$, and both differentials are isometries carrying the unit future normal of $S$ to the unit future normal of $\Phi(S)$ ([[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] clause (e); [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]] for the uniqueness of the normal). By uniqueness of geodesics with given initial data ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]) the two geodesics coincide, so $\psi(y)=\varphi(y)$.

(The patched map.) Define $\Psi:U\cup N_0\to M'$ by $\Psi:=\psi$ on $U$ and $\Psi:=\varphi$ on $N_0$. This is well defined by step 4.1 and smooth and is a data-fixing isometric immersion preserving the time orientation and the matter fields, because these are local properties and hold for $\psi$ on $U$ and for $\varphi$ on $N_0$ ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clauses (b)-(c), [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a)).

($U\cup N_0$ is a development.) By [L6] every causal curve in $U\cup N_0$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N_0$ meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; $U\cup N_0\subseteq M$ is open with the restricted metric, time orientation and matter fields, the field equations hold (they are local and hold on $M$), and $j:\Sigma\to U\cup N_0$ is an embedding with the induced data $(h,K,\psi_0)$. Hence $U\cup N_0$ is a development of the same data ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)); in particular it is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $\Sigma$ by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

($\Psi$ is a development embedding.) By step 5.1, $\Psi$ is a data-fixing isometric immersion of the development $U\cup N_0$ into $M'$; hence it is injective and a diffeomorphism onto the open set $\Psi(U\cup N_0)$ by [L5].

(Strictly larger.) Pick $x\in S\cap\partial U$ (nonempty by [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] clause (b)). Then $x\in S\subseteq N_0$ and $x\notin U$, so $N_0\not\subseteq U$ and $U\subsetneq U\cup N_0$. Thus $(U\cup N_0,\Psi)$ is a common subdevelopment of $M$ and $M'$ strictly larger than $(U,\varphi)$, contradicting the maximality of $(U,\varphi)$ assumed in the statement.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. **(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. smooth sections $\psi^i$ of the tensor bundles over $M$ of the types
   $r_i$ of the sector;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;

equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$, so $\varphi$ carries
   the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, that is, $\psi'{}^i(\varphi(p))=(d\varphi_p)^{\otimes}\psi^i(p)$
   for every $i$ and $p$, with the natural action on tensor fields of each
   listed type.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,\psi_0)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and

$\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$, and:

1. every causal curve in $N$ is, in the coordinates $(s,t)$, of the form

   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in

**Data.** Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $K$. The normal convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Specify one fixed covariant matter model, consisting of a finite list of smooth tensor fields $\psi$, fixed equations $\mathcal E(g,\psi)=0$ and a fixed stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\psi)$, with pullback by local diffeomorphisms commuting with the equations and stress. Fix its complete smooth Cauchy data $d$: these determine all independent matter initial variables, not only the normal stress projections. Initial tensors with normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb R\nu\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $g_0(a\nu+X,b\nu+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. In a development, identify $a\nu+X$ with $an+dj(X)$.

An admissible fixed coupled model is one satisfying the complete initialization, hyperbolic reduction, recovery and comparison hypotheses of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]], or a specified independent local existence and uniqueness reduction such as the dust branch below. The same fixed model, complete data and admissibility conditions are used in every comparison and at every restart. Admissibility includes the applicability of its supplied complete-data local existence and geometric uniqueness theorem to the data realized on each spacelike restart surface of the compared solutions. This must be checked for the actual model and surface; it is not inferred from stress conservation. This class includes the following four concrete branches; they do not exhaust it.

1. **Vacuum:** no matter fields, $\mathcal T=0$, and empty matter data.
2. **Scalar field:** fix one smooth potential $V$ and one normalization $K_\phi>0$. The field is $\varphi$, its equation is $\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$, its stress is the expression in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] clause (c), and its complete data are $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ with $\pi_0=n(\varphi)|_\Sigma$. The fixed potential has no sign restriction ([[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]).
3. **Strict barotropic fluid:** fix a smooth EOS $P:J\to\mathbb R$ on an open interval with $\epsilon+P(\epsilon)>0$ and $0<P'(\epsilon)<1$. The fields are $\epsilon\in J$ and future unit velocity $u$, the stress is $(\epsilon+P(\epsilon))u^\flat\otimes u^\flat+P(\epsilon)g$, and the equations are the continuity and Euler equations of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] clause (c), with this fixed EOS. Complete data are $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$, where $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, equivalently the bundle velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(\nu+v_0)$. No small-tilt restriction is imposed ([[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]]).
4. **Geodesic nonnegative dust:** the fields are an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon\ge0$ and a smooth future unit timelike field $u$, including on $\{\varepsilon=0\}$. Set $\mathcal T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$ and require both $\nabla_u u=0$ and $u(\varepsilon)+\varepsilon\nabla_a u^a=0$ everywhere. Complete data are $(\varepsilon_0,U_0)$, with $\varepsilon_0\ge0$ and prescribed smooth future unit bundle velocity $U_0$, equivalently arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt. On positive-density regions this is [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]] with its density parameter equal to $\varepsilon$. Through empty regions the geodesic velocity is separately prescribed and matched; conservation of stress alone is not substituted for this full system. For a fixed $c>0$, the mass-normalized theorem [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] applies with $\rho_0=\varepsilon_0/c^2$ and reconstructs $\varepsilon=c^2\rho$.

Require the constraints for the initial stress $T_0$ computed from this complete data on $\mathcal V$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(\nu,\nu),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(\nu,\cdot).$$
These use the convention of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]. Equality of data includes equality of the model, constants, potential or EOS, and every component of $d$.

The local Cauchy-development and uniqueness suppliers for vacuum, scalar and strict fluid are the fixed-model theorem [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] and the two concrete branch theorems above. Its harmonic route requires the same fixed extraction/reconstruction rules and smooth symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family for every compared physical solution, a positive time matrix on an admissible open state set, complete compatible initialization from $(h,K,d)$, propagation of auxiliary compatibility with recovery of the full matter equations on the reduced solution, and stress conservation on that reduced solution before Einstein recovery. These are the three explicit hypotheses of that theorem; conservation alone does not supply a Cauchy evolution law. Dust uses its independent common-flow/parallel-frame initialization, hyperbolic reduction, subsidiary recovery and uniqueness of [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]], rather than being asserted to satisfy the harmonic metric-first-derivative matter contract. Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are carried wherever these local theorems are invoked. Every additional fixed coupled model must supply the same complete-data local existence, admissibility, recovery and uniqueness obligations before it is used. This definition makes no local or global existence assertion.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. the smooth tensor fields $\psi$ of the fixed model over $M$;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;

   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one

   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and

3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, with the natural pullback action on every listed tensor type (and the inverse differential on contravariant slots). Equality includes every listed field, including the prescribed dust velocity at zero density.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,d)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

Suppose $(s,\sigma):U\to I\times B_R$ is a diffeomorphism of an open set $U\subseteq M$, satisfying:

**(C1)** $\partial_s$ is future timelike and every $s$-level is spacelike;

**(C2)** there is $K\ge1$ such that $|d\sigma(v)|\le Kds(v)$ for every nonzero future causal vector $v$ based in $U$.

Write $S=s^{-1}(0)$, and compute the domains of dependence intrinsically in $U$:
$$D^+_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D^-_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\}.$$
Here inextendibility means absence of an endpoint limit in the specified open submanifold, and Cauchy intersection means exactly one parameter visit ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). Then:

**(a)** $D^+_U(S)\subseteq\{s\ge0\}$ and $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$.

**(b)** The corrected open collar
$$Q=\{q\in U:|\sigma(q)|+K|s(q)|<R\}$$
is a neighborhood of the entire slice $S$ in $U$ and is contained in $D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)$; more precisely $Q\cap\{s>0\}\subseteq D^+_U(S)$ and $Q\cap\{s<0\}\subseteq D^-_U(S)$.

**(c)** The open set $W=\operatorname{int}_U(D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S))$ contains $Q$, and $S$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(W,g|_W,N|_W)$. Consequently $W$ is globally hyperbolic by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(d) Generic spacelike and noncompact scope.** For every smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subseteq M$ without boundary there exist an open neighborhood $U_\Sigma$ of $\Sigma$, a smooth positive function $\delta:\Sigma\to(0,\infty)$, and a diffeomorphism
$$F:\Omega\to U_\Sigma,\qquad\Omega=\{(s,x)\in\mathbb R\times\Sigma:|s|<\delta(x)\},\qquad F(0,x)=x,$$
such that $s$ is temporal and $F_*\partial_s$ is future timelike. The intrinsic set $W_\Sigma=\operatorname{int}_{U_\Sigma}(D^+_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma)\cup D^-_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma))$ is an open neighborhood in which $\Sigma$ is Cauchy, hence is globally hyperbolic. Neither compactness nor global acausality of $\Sigma$ in $M$ is assumed. No positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause
(a), with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$. Let
$\varphi:M\to M'$ be a smooth map with $\varphi^*(g')=g$, with
$g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$, with
$\varphi\circ j=j'$ and $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$ (so $\varphi$ is a future isometric immersion fixing the complete data and matching every matter field).
Then:

**(a)** $d\varphi_p:T_pM\to T_{\varphi(p)}M'$ is an isomorphism for every
$p\in M$;

**(b)** $\varphi$ is injective, hence a diffeomorphism onto the open subset
$\varphi(M)\subseteq M'$ and therefore a development embedding in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c);

**(c)** if $M$ is connected and $\psi_1,\psi_2:M\to M'$ are two such
data-fixing isometric immersions, then $\psi_1=\psi_2$; in particular every
data-fixing self-isometry of a connected development is the identity of $M$.

Throughout, for a smooth map $\psi:N\to N'$ between smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds write $\psi^*(g')=g$ when $g_p(v,w)=g'_{\psi(p)}(d\psi_pv,d\psi_pw)$
for all $p\in N$ and $v,w\in T_pN$; such a map is an **isometric immersion**
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). Let $\nabla,\nabla'$ be
the metric-selected connections ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let geodesics
and exponential maps be those of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]].

**(a) Rigidity.** Let $N$ be connected and let
$\psi_1,\psi_2:N\to N'$ be isometric immersions with
$\psi_1(p)=\psi_2(p)$ and $d\psi_1(p)=d\psi_2(p)$ for some $p\in N$. Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$, that is, $\psi_1(q)=\psi_2(q)$ and $d\psi_1(q)=d\psi_2(q)$
for every $q\in N$.

**(b) Data-fixing embeddings have equal differentials on the initial surface.**
Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$, $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ and $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ be
as in [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a),
and let $\psi_1,\psi_2:U\to M'$ be development embeddings in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c). Then
$d\psi_1=d\psi_2$ at every point of $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$.

**(c) Agreement on overlaps.** Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$
be developments of the same data, and let $(U_1,\psi_1)$ and $(U_2,\psi_2)$ be
common subdevelopments in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$ on $U_1\cap U_2$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed
boundary point in the sense of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]:
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$
Fix a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $p$
([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let
$p_1\ll p\ll p_2$ be points of $C$ such that $W:=I^+(p_1)\cap I^-(p_2)$
satisfies $\overline W\subseteq C$ (possible: strong causality at $p$ supplies
a neighbourhood $V_2\subseteq C$ of $p$ such that every causal curve with
both endpoints in $V_2$ is contained in $C$, and then
$\overline W\subseteq J^+(p_1)\cap J^-(p_2)\subseteq C$ for $p_1,p_2\in V_2$
by the same argument). Then $W$ is open, causally convex, $p\in W$, and
$\overline W$ is compact. Let $q\in W\cap I^+(p)$ be a point with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W,$$

([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from

$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in

$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

following properties. Define $X:=\nabla\tau_q/g(\nabla\tau_q,\nabla\tau_q)$

flow, and put
$$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M,\qquad F(s,t):=\phi_t(s),\qquad N:=F\bigl(S\times(-\delta,\delta)\bigr).$$

   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric

   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;

$$\{F(s,u):u\text{ between }0\text{ and }t_y,\ u\ne0\}$$
is contained in $U$. The base belongs to $U\cup C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, and the full segment including the base is contained in $U$ whenever $s\in U$. In particular, if $t_y<0$ then also $s\in U$. If $\Theta:N\to M'$ is a time-orientation-preserving local isometry with $\Theta|_S=\Phi|_S$, where $\Phi$ is the smooth extension of the common-subdevelopment map $\varphi$, then $\Theta=\varphi$ on $N\cap U$;
4. the tube can be chosen inside any prescribed open neighbourhood $O\subseteq W$ of the whole $S$, and below any prescribed positive continuous width ceiling on $S$. $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.
